# Configuration reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-schema.ts from the Zod schema and scripts/config-descriptions.ts. Do not edit. -->

ReleaseRay reads one optional file, `.releaseray/config.yml` (the `config` input changes the path). Every key is optional except `version`. Values merge in this order, later winning: built-in defaults, the file, Action inputs.

Add this first line so editors check the file as you type:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cristobalmitchell/releaseray/v1/schema/releaseray.schema.json
```

Rules that span keys (persona names in outputs, internal personas on published outputs, provider settings) are checked by `mode: validate-config` and at the start of every run. Credentials never go in this file: name them by environment variable.

## Version

The config format version.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `version` | `1` |  | Always 1. |

## Range

How the commits for a release are chosen. Everything comes from local git, so the checkout needs `fetch-depth: 0`.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `range.tagPattern` | string | `v*` | Glob over tag names that count as releases, as `git tag --list` reads it. |
| `range.includePrereleases` | boolean | `false` | Let a prerelease tag be the previous tag of a release. |
| `range.allowNonAncestor` | boolean | `false` | Allow an explicit `from` that is not an ancestor of `to`. The `allow-non-ancestor` input sets it for one run. |
| `range.fallbackToCommits` | boolean | `true` | Write notes from commit messages when no commit names a pull request. |
| `range.maxPullRequests` | integer 1–5000 | `250` | Stop before any REST call when a range names more pull requests than this; set `from` or narrow the window. |

## Classification

Categories, the labels and commit types that map to them, and what to leave out. Configured categories merge over the nine built-ins by id.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `classification.categories` | list of object | `[]` | Categories to add, or built-in categories to change, by id. |
| `classification.categories[].id` | string |  | Slug. A built-in id (breaking, security, features, improvements, fixes, performance, deprecations, docs, internal) changes that category. |
| `classification.categories[].title` | string |  | Name the classifier and the model see. Default: the built-in title, or the id in words. |
| `classification.categories[].labels` | list of string |  | Pull request labels that put a change here: exact names (any case) or `/regex/flags`. |
| `classification.categories[].conventionalTypes` | list of string |  | Conventional-commit types that map here, such as feat, fix or ci. |
| `classification.categories[].internal` | boolean |  | Hide this category from personas that exclude internal changes. |
| `classification.conventionalCommits` | boolean | `true` | Read conventional-commit prefixes in titles and commits. |
| `classification.fallbackCategory` | string | `improvements` | Category for changes with no other signal; unknown model sections merge into its section. |
| `classification.exclude.labels` | list of string | `["skip-release-notes"]` | Pull requests with any of these labels are left out (exact names or `/regex/`). |
| `classification.exclude.authors` | list of string | `[]` | Pull requests by these logins are left out, such as `renovate[bot]`. |
| `classification.exclude.titlePatterns` | list of string | `[]` | Regular expressions (`source` or `/source/flags`) matched against commit subjects and pull request titles; matches are left out. |

## Enrichment

What is fetched from GitHub besides each pull request's title and labels. More enrichment means more REST requests and a longer prompt.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enrichment.bodies` | boolean | `true` | Send pull request and issue bodies to the model. |
| `enrichment.linkedIssues` | boolean | `true` | Fetch issues that pull request bodies link to (one request each). |
| `enrichment.maxLinkedIssues` | integer 0–500 | `100` | Most linked issues fetched per release. |
| `enrichment.comments` | boolean | `false` | Fetch comments and reviews (two requests per pull request, one per issue). Off by default: it costs requests and widens prompt-injection exposure. |
| `enrichment.commentAuthorAssociations` | list of `OWNER` \| `MEMBER` \| `COLLABORATOR` | `["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"]` | Keep only comments from these author associations. |
| `enrichment.maxBodyChars` | integer 0–20000 | `4000` | Characters of each body sent to the model. |

## Personas

Who the notes are written for. Entries merge over the built-ins `engineer`, `internal` and `customer` by slug; other slugs add personas.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `personas` | list of object |  | Persona entries, merged over the built-ins by slug. |
| `personas[].slug` | string |  | Lowercase id. engineer, internal and customer change a built-in; anything else adds a persona. |
| `personas[].extends` | `engineer` \| `internal` \| `customer` |  | Start a new persona from a built-in's rules and sections. |
| `personas[].name` | string |  | Display name in the summary. |
| `personas[].description` | string |  | Who this persona is for; sent to the model. |
| `personas[].enabled` | boolean | `true` | Set false to stop generating this persona. |
| `personas[].visibility` | `public` \| `internal` |  | internal personas are withheld from public outputs and from public repositories' summaries. Default: internal for `internal` and personas extending it. |
| `personas[].tone.formality` | integer 0–100 |  | 0 casual to 100 formal. Default 50; 0 is kept. |
| `personas[].tone.technicalDepth` | integer 0–100 |  | 0 plain language to 100 technical. Default 50. |
| `personas[].tone.enthusiasm` | integer 0–100 |  | 0 neutral to 100 enthusiastic. Default 30. |
| `personas[].tone.detail` | integer 0–100 |  | 0 brief to 100 comprehensive. Default 50. |
| `personas[].instructions` | string |  | Extra instructions for the model, up to 2,000 characters. |
| `personas[].instructionsFile` | string |  | Like `instructions`, from a file under `.releaseray/`. |
| `personas[].include.identifiers` | boolean |  | Show pull request and issue numbers and commit SHAs. |
| `personas[].include.breakingChanges` | boolean |  | Ask for breaking changes. |
| `personas[].include.migrationGuides` | boolean |  | Ask for migration guides. |
| `personas[].include.highlights` | boolean |  | Render the Highlights section. |
| `personas[].include.upgradeInstructions` | boolean |  | Render upgrade instructions. |
| `personas[].include.contributors` | boolean |  | Render the contributors line (from pull request authors). |
| `personas[].sections` | list of object |  | The sections to write, in order (at most 15). Replaces the persona's default sections. |
| `personas[].sections[].id` | string |  | Slug. A standard section id (breaking-changes, features, bug-fixes, …) keeps its category mapping. |
| `personas[].sections[].name` | string |  | Heading in the notes. |
| `personas[].sections[].description` | string |  | What belongs in this section; sent to the model. |
| `personas[].sections[].categories` | list of string | `[]` | Category ids this section collects. Empty: the standard section's categories, or the category with the same id. |
| `personas[].sections[].enabled` | boolean | `true` | Set false to hide the section. |
| `personas[].excludeCategories` | list of string |  | Category ids this persona never shows. The built-in customer persona excludes internal. |

## Outputs

Where the notes go. The job summary and workspace files are on by default; the GitHub Release is written when `publish` resolves to true.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `outputs.summary.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Write notes, usage and completeness to the job summary. |
| `outputs.summary.personas` | `all` \| list of string | `all` | `all`, or the slugs to show. |
| `outputs.files.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Write `<dir>/<key>/<persona>.md` and `notes.json` in the workspace. |
| `outputs.files.dir` | string | `.releaseray/notes` | Directory for the workspace files, relative to the checkout. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Write a block into the GitHub Release when `publish` resolves to true. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.persona` | string | `engineer` | The persona whose notes go into the release. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.mode` | `section` \| `replace` | `section` | `section` appends a marked block and keeps other text; `replace` writes the whole body. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.onHumanEdit` | `skip` \| `overwrite` | `skip` | `skip` leaves a block a person edited; `overwrite` replaces it. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.createIfMissing` | boolean | `false` | Create the release when none exists for the tag. The `create-release` input sets it for one run. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.nameTemplate` | string | `Release {{tag}}` | Name of a created release; `{{tag}}` is the tag. |
| `outputs.githubRelease.prerelease` | `auto` \| boolean | `auto` | Prerelease flag of a created release; `auto` follows SemVer. |
| `outputs.changelog.enabled` | boolean | `false` | Write a marked entry into the CHANGELOG file in the workspace. |
| `outputs.changelog.path` | string | `CHANGELOG.md` | CHANGELOG path, relative to the checkout. |
| `outputs.changelog.persona` | string | `engineer` | The persona whose notes go into the CHANGELOG. |
| `outputs.changelog.onHumanEdit` | `skip` \| `overwrite` | `skip` | `skip` leaves an entry a person wrote or edited; `overwrite` replaces it. |
| `outputs.changelog.push` | boolean | `false` | Commit and push the entry. The `push` input sets it for one run. |
| `outputs.changelog.branch` | string |  | Branch to push to. Default: the checked-out branch, else the default branch. |
| `outputs.changelog.commitMessage` | string | `docs(changelog): {{key}}` | Commit subject; `{{key}}` is the release key. |
| `outputs.changelog.author.name` | string |  | Commit author name. Default: github-actions[bot]. |
| `outputs.changelog.author.email` | string |  | Commit author email. |
| `outputs.notify` | list of object | `[]` | Slack, Teams and Intercom, posted after the GitHub Release and CHANGELOG when `publish` is true. Each entry posts when the primary target (the GitHub Release, else the CHANGELOG) changed in this run, so a re-run that changes nothing sends nothing. |
| `outputs.notify[].type` | `slack` \| `teams` \| `intercom` |  | `slack`, `teams` or `intercom`. |
| `outputs.notify[].persona` | string |  | The persona whose notes are sent. |
| `outputs.notify[].webhookUrlEnv` | string |  | Slack and Teams: the environment variable holding the incoming webhook URL. Slack URLs must be on `hooks.slack.com` or `hooks.slack-gov.com`; Teams URLs on `*.webhook.office.com` or `*.office365.com`. |
| `outputs.notify[].when` | `primary-changed` \| `always` | `primary-changed` | `primary-changed` posts only when the primary target changed in this run; `always` posts on every publishing run. The `notify` input overrides it for one run. |
| `outputs.notify[].apiKeyEnv` | string |  | Intercom: the environment variable holding the access token. |
| `outputs.notify[].collectionId` | string |  | Intercom: the Help Center collection new articles go into. |
| `outputs.notify[].state` | `draft` \| `published` | `draft` | Intercom: the state of a created or updated article. |
| `outputs.notify[].titleTemplate` | string | `Release {{key}}` | Intercom: the article title; `{{key}}` is the release key. The article is found again by this title, so one renamed by hand is created anew. |
| `outputs.allowInternalOutputs` | boolean | `false` | Allow an internal persona on the GitHub Release or CHANGELOG. |
| `outputs.allowInternalOnPublicRepo` | boolean | `false` | Show internal personas in the summary and files of a public repository. |

## LLM

The model provider and its limits. Keys come from environment variables, never from this file.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `llm.provider` | `openai` \| `bedrock` \| `anthropic` | `openai` | `openai` (or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), `bedrock` or `anthropic`. |
| `llm.model` | string |  | Model id. Default: gpt-5-mini on openai, Claude Haiku 4.5 on bedrock, claude-opus-5-5 on anthropic. Bedrock accepts inference-profile ARNs. |
| `llm.baseUrl` | string |  | OpenAI-compatible endpoint (openai only). |
| `llm.region` | string |  | AWS region (bedrock only; required there). |
| `llm.maxCompletionTokens` | integer 256–65536 | `16384` | Most tokens per model response. |
| `llm.maxInputTokens` | integer 1000–9007199254740991 | `200000` | Most input tokens per persona call, estimated at 4 characters each and checked before any call. |
| `llm.concurrency` | integer 1–10 | `3` | Persona calls in parallel. |
| `llm.retries` | integer 0–5 | `3` | Times to ask again after invalid output; transient errors retry separately. |
| `llm.pricing.inputPer1M` | number ≥ 0 |  | USD per million input tokens, for a model the built-in table lacks. |
| `llm.pricing.outputPer1M` | number ≥ 0 |  | USD per million output tokens. |

## GitHub requests

The REST request budget and what to do when a release would exceed it.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `github.maxRequests` | integer 1–9007199254740991 |  | Request cap for a run. Default: 90% of the token's hourly core limit. |
| `github.concurrency` | integer 1–10 | `1` | REST reads in parallel. Writes are always serial. |
| `github.onBudgetExceeded` | `fail` \| `wait` \| `degrade` | `fail` | When the estimate does not fit: `fail` (exit 3), `wait` for the reset within `maxWaitMinutes`, or `degrade` (drop comments, then linked issues). Also governs `llm.maxInputTokens`. |
| `github.maxWaitMinutes` | integer 0–300 | `0` | Longest wait for a rate-limit reset. Raise the job's `timeout-minutes` to match. |

## Sanitizing

What is removed from published text.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sanitize.allowedDomains` | list of string | `["github.com","gitlab.com"]` | Hosts (and their subdomains) whose links are kept; other links are redacted. |
| `sanitize.redactPaths` | boolean | `true` | Remove file paths from published text. |

## Rendering

How the Markdown looks.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render.emoji` | boolean | `true` | Emoji in section headings. |
| `render.compareLink` | boolean | `true` | End with a compare link from the previous tag. |
